doNotStore.description: Process the content without saving it on our servers. The item is still created and appears in the review queue, analytics and author history with its moderation results, but its content is empty, so reviewers cannot see what was submitted.

contextId.description: For example the ID of a chat room or a post

metadata.description: Any metadata you want to store with the content

value.description: The text you'd like to analyze. We recommend to submit plain text or HTML

status.description: Success if the request was successful

quota_usage.description: The quota usage of the request

flagged.description: Whether the content was flagged by any models

external_id.description: The author's ID from your system

until.description: The timestamp until which they are blocked if the author is suspended.

reason.description: The moderators reason why the author was blocked or suspended.

block.description: Block or suspension details, if applicable. Null if the author is enabled.

manual.description: True if the trust level was set manually by a moderator

author.description: The author of the content if your account has authors enabled. Requires you to send authorId when submitting content.

content_moderated.description: Whether the content was moderated or not. Same as `content` !== `original`

unicode_spoofing.description: Whether the content is using look-alike characters. Often used by spammers.

data_found.description: Whether any entity matchers found data for the content

content.description: The content after moderation. With all mask replacements applied and look-alike characters replaced with the original characters.

get.description:
Open a WebSocket to moderate live voice/call audio in real time. Speech is transcribed and each finalized utterance is moderated by your enabled text policies; you receive a verdict per utterance as it's spoken.

**This is a WebSocket upgrade, not a regular HTTP call.** The request body below documents the frames you *send* over the socket; the `101` response documents the events you *receive*.

- **Auth:** `Authorization: Bearer <api_key>` on the upgrade. A missing/invalid key closes `4401`; voice not enabled on the plan/channel closes `4403`.
- **Subprotocol:** request `moderationapi.v1`.
- **Flow:** send one `start` frame, then `media` frames as audio arrives, then `stop` (or disconnect). You receive `session.started`, `utterance.final` per utterance, optional `utterance.partial`/`warning`, and `session.ended`.
- **Close codes:** `1000` normal · `1011` server error · `4400` bad request · `4401` auth failed · `4403` voice not enabled · `4429` concurrency limit.

See the [Real-time voice guide](https://docs.moderationapi.com/content-moderation/real-time-voice) for the full walkthrough and code examples.

post.description: Fired when an author transitions to the `blocked` status. The `data.object` is the action_performed record that drove the transition, with the author and triggering action nested as inline resources.

200.description: Acknowledge receipt. Any 2xx status closes the delivery as successful; non-2xx triggers retry with exponential backoff.

post.description: Fired when an author transitions back to the `enabled` status. May fire automatically when a temporary suspension expires (the auto-unblock worker runs the `AUTHOR_UNBLOCK` action).

200.description: Acknowledge receipt. Any 2xx status closes the delivery as successful; non-2xx triggers retry with exponential backoff.

post.description: Fired when an author is suspended for a finite period. The `block.until` field on the nested author indicates when the suspension expires.

200.description: Acknowledge receipt. Any 2xx status closes the delivery as successful; non-2xx triggers retry with exponential backoff.

post.description: Fired when public author fields (name, email, profile picture, metadata, etc.) change. Status transitions have their own dedicated events and do **not** trigger this.

200.description: Acknowledge receipt. Any 2xx status closes the delivery as successful; non-2xx triggers retry with exponential backoff.

post.description: Fired when an author's resolved trust level (manual override, falling back to computed) transitions to a new value. Does not fire for no-op recomputes.

200.description: Acknowledge receipt. Any 2xx status closes the delivery as successful; non-2xx triggers retry with exponential backoff.

post.summary: A custom action was performed on an author
post.description: Fired when an `AUTHOR_CUSTOM` moderation action runs against an author. Same shape as the lifecycle events (`author.blocked`, `author.suspended`, `author.unblocked`).

200.description: Acknowledge receipt. Any 2xx status closes the delivery as successful; non-2xx triggers retry with exponential backoff.

post.description: Fired when a moderator marks a queue item as resolved (checked off the queue).

200.description: Acknowledge receipt. Any 2xx status closes the delivery as successful; non-2xx triggers retry with exponential backoff.

post.summary: A custom action was performed on a queue item
post.description: Fired when a **custom** moderation action runs against a queue item. The `data.object` is the action_performed record with the related action, item, author, and queue nested as inline resources. Built-in actions (reject, allow) have dedicated events — see `queue_item.rejected` and `queue_item.allowed` instead.

200.description: Acknowledge receipt. Any 2xx status closes the delivery as successful; non-2xx triggers retry with exponential backoff.

post.description: Fired when the built-in **reject** action runs against a queue item. Same shape as `queue_item.action`. Customers who want every action firing should subscribe to both this and the other built-in/custom events; subscribing only to `queue_item.action` no longer catches built-in events.

200.description: Acknowledge receipt. Any 2xx status closes the delivery as successful; non-2xx triggers retry with exponential backoff.

post.description: Fired when the built-in **allow** action runs against a queue item. Same shape as `queue_item.action`. Customers who want every action firing should subscribe to both this and the other built-in/custom events.

200.description: Acknowledge receipt. Any 2xx status closes the delivery as successful; non-2xx triggers retry with exponential backoff.
